concepts.learning_objective: Find the number each person calls out when the rule is 'count the taller people in front of you'.
Judge whether statements about the called-out numbers are always, sometimes or never true.

topics.title: Picking Parity: Sums of Even and Odd Numbers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain parity using the idea of arranging a number in pairs.
Decide the parity of a sum from the parity and count of the numbers added.
Use the fact that two consecutive numbers have different parity.

topics.title: Parity in Grids and Expressions
topics.ncert_sections: 6.2 (Small Squares in Grids, Parity of Expressions)

concepts.learning_objective: Find the parity of the number of small squares in a grid without multiplying.
Identify expressions that are always even, always odd, or either.
Use 2n and 2n - 1 to find the nth even and nth odd number.

topics.title: Grid Sums and 3 x 3 Magic Squares

concepts.learning_objective: Use the smallest and largest possible sums and the total 45 to reason about grids filled with 1-9.
Explain why a 1-9 magic square has magic sum 15, centre 5, and 1 and 9 in middle positions.

topics.title: Generalising Magic Squares and Their History
topics.ncert_sections: 6.3 (Generalising a 3 x 3 Magic Square, Magic Squares in History and Culture)

concepts.learning_objective: Use the centre number m to describe a magic square and its magic sum 3m.
Predict the new magic sum when every number of a magic square is changed in the same way.
Recall the Chautisa Yantra and other magic squares in Indian history and culture.
Extend the Virahanka sequence by adding the two previous terms.
Count rhythms of short and long syllables, or 1-and-2 step paths, using the Virahanka numbers.
Recall who first described these numbers and the parity pattern of the sequence.
Solve simple cryptarithms by reasoning about place value and carries.
Apply parity to decide everyday puzzles such as switch toggling.
